sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose of the role words
sections.what: Header comment explaining the word lists: they accept native-language and extra English wording for approved roles, but each word must state its role (a final cost, a realised completion, an original baseline) rather than a plan or estimate.
sections.why: The comment records a user decision dated 2026-10-29.
sections.watch_out: Native words match without a left boundary, so a short stem may match inside an unrelated word.

sections.name: rx (part 1)
sections.title: Budget and cost word lists
sections.what: Builds the word patterns for approved budgets, final costs and estimates, in English and the source languages. Each pattern combines whole English words with native stems.
sections.why: Likely reason: English words need whole-word matching, while compound native words need stem matching.
sections.watch_out: The exact stems in these lists decide what is accepted, so a missing stem causes a valid sentence to be rejected.

sections.name: rx (part 2)
sections.title: Completion and future-date word lists
sections.what: Defines the words that show a completion has happened (in service, commissioned, taken into operation) and the words that mark a date as a plan or future event.
sections.why: The comment says future or planned dates must never count as completions.
sections.watch_out: Future words are blocked anywhere in a quote, so a quote mentioning a future phase next to a completed one may be rejected.

sections.name: statesFuture
sections.title: Checks a quote for future wording
sections.what: Returns true when a quote uses future or planned wording, after removing schedule phrases such as as scheduled and on schedule, which describe outcomes.
sections.why: Likely reason: those schedule phrases would otherwise trigger the future-word check wrongly.
sections.watch_out: Only the listed schedule phrases are removed, so a new idiom with a future-sounding word is treated as a plan.

sections.name: MONTH_NAMES
sections.title: Month names in source languages
sections.what: Lists the names of each month in English and the source languages (including Finnish and Icelandic forms), indexed by month position.
sections.why: Likely reason: dates written in these languages must be checked against the right month.
sections.watch_out: The list is indexed by position, so a name placed in the wrong row would silently check the wrong month.

summary: Holds the word lists that decide whether a quote states a budget, a final cost, a realised completion or an original baseline, in English and in several source languages.
purpose: Makes the research checks accept valid native-language wording and reject plans, forecasts and estimates.
why: The header comment records a user decision dated 2026-10-29 to accept native and extra English role wording while still requiring the role to be stated.
how: Builds pattern matchers from English words (with whole-word matching) and native stems (matched inside longer words). Defines lists for baseline budgets, final costs, estimates, completions, future wording and baseline dates. Provides a check for future wording with schedule phrases removed, and month names in each language.
inputs: Text of a quote, to be tested against the patterns.
outputs: Yes or no matches, and a list of month names indexed by month.
risks: Native stems match without a left boundary, so a short stem can match unrelated words. A future-tense word anywhere in a quote can block an otherwise valid completion.
debug: If a valid sentence is rejected, find its key word and check the matching list here. If a date is misread, check the month name rows. Matching tests are in roleWords.test.ts.
